sections.h2: What the Recorder of Deeds does
sections.html:
Land transfers and ownership changes in Jefferson County, Missouri, are kept on public record here. Staff record deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, plats, restrictions, surveys and affidavits, and the office also issues marriage licenses. Military discharge papers (DD214) and tax liens can be recorded on request.

  • Address: 729 Maple Street, Hillsboro, MO 63050.
  • Phone: 636-797-5414.
  • Cutoff: a document presented after 4:30 PM is processed the following business day.
  • Location rule: a document goes on record in the county where the land sits, so this office cannot record property in another county.

Drafting is outside the office's role. Employees will not write a document, supply a blank form or notarize what they record, and they send owners to a title company or real estate attorney. Bring finished, signed and notarized papers to the counter.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before it is accepted
sections.html:
Missouri's section 59.310 sets the rules, and the county posts them on its recording requirements page. Expect a refusal if your document misses one of the following.

  • Single-sided, unbound pages of white or light paper, 20 pound weight or heavier, with dark ink and type of 8 point or larger.
  • Room for the recorder's stamp: 3 inches left blank at the top of page one, and three-fourths of an inch or more on the remaining edges.
  • Below that margin on page one: the title, date, grantor names with marital status, grantee names, any statutory addresses, the legal description and any reference book and page.
  • A true legal description, such as lot, block and plat, or metes and bounds. A street address never counts.
  • A notary acknowledgment with seal and signature, plus a mailing address for at least one grantee.

The format rules can be bypassed for a $25 surcharge, which lets a noncompliant paper go on record anyway. Some categories never face the rules: documents signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, papers signed abroad, certified copies and court judgments.

Sellers of acreage face one more local step. A transfer deed describing under 10 acres outside any city, or only part of a subdivision lot, needs an exemption from the county Planning and Zoning Department first, or the recorder will not take it.

sections.h2: What it costs to record or copy a document
sections.html:
Lawmakers in Jefferson City set the fees, and the counter prices each document by how many pages it has. Payment comes first, by cash or by a check payable to the Jefferson County Recorder of Deeds. The county links a Real Estate Recording Fees PDF among its recorder quick links, or ask your title company what your deed will cost.

Recorder charges in Jefferson County
ServiceCharge
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page
Certification of a copy$1
Deed that fails the format rules$25 extra
Pay-per-search online records site$8.95 per search, $1 per page copied

A phone order by card adds a $1 processing fee from the card company, plus postage. Part of every fee goes to the State Land Survey Office, which uses the money to update state surveys and maintain vital land records.

sections.h2: What happens after a deed reaches the office
sections.html:
There are six steps, which explains why a closing package can take a day or two to come back.

  1. Staff check dates, signatures, name spellings and the acknowledgment.
  2. The document is accepted and priced by page count.
  3. It receives a date and time stamp and a document number, and page one is sealed.
  4. It is scanned.
  5. It is indexed under the grantor and grantee names.
  6. A second check confirms the index entry, then the document is mailed to the address provided. Including a self-addressed envelope speeds that return.

A rejected deed goes back to the preparer with the reason. If a deed is being re-recorded, it must be acknowledged again and must say why.

sections.h2: Which deed fits my sale or transfer?
sections.html:
The recorder's FAQ describes three common kinds. With a warranty deed, a seller conveys title and promises that no liens from the seller or earlier owners cloud it. A quit claim deed lets current owners add or remove an owner, change a name or correct an error. A beneficiary deed, also called a time of death deed, records what the owner wants to happen after death.

A deed of trust is the mortgage lien. Each new loan or refinance records a new one, and when the debt is paid the lender must record a deed of release that cites the original document number. If an old lien was never released, ask the lender for that paper before closing.

The office recommends an attorney or title company for any deed, though an owner may write their own if it meets Missouri's formatting rules.

In person, the vault index lists grantors (sellers) and grantees (buyers) alphabetically. Look up your own name as grantee to find the deed from your purchase, then follow the book and page number it gives. Online there are three routes: a pay-per-search site, a Laredo subscription covering records from April 1985 to the present, and the hosted COTT Systems site for older records.

If the buyer's name draws a blank, try the seller's name too, since each recording is indexed under both parties. Write down the document number and the book and page for your files.

Laredo requires a signed user agreement from the Recorder. Losing your deed does not cost you ownership, because the recording is the main evidence of title and a certified copy can replace the original.

The recorder quick links also include a Property Fraud Alert notice. Owners of paid-off houses who get contacted about a deed transfer should read it.

sections.h2: The documents in a typical closing
sections.html:
A house sale in Jefferson County often produces three recordings back to back: a deed of release for the seller's old loan, the warranty deed to the buyer, and the buyer's new deed of trust. Each is checked, priced by page count and indexed separately, so one closing can add several entries to the grantor and grantee index.

Ask your title company which documents it plans to present and in what order. Communities whose deeds are filed here include Arnold, Festus, De Soto, Crystal City, Pevely, Herculaneum, Hillsboro and Byrnes Mill, while Eureka is mostly on the St. Louis County side.

If you sell for cash, expect fewer pieces of paper. With no buyer loan, the closing usually needs only the release of your old loan and the deed to the buyer, which also means fewer fees at the recorder's counter.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Jefferson County, Missouri?
faqs.a: At the Recorder of Deeds office, 729 Maple Street, Hillsboro. Phone 636-797-5414 before you go. Anything handed in after 4:30 PM is held until the next business day.

faqs.q: Can the recorder write my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. The office does not prepare documents, give legal advice, supply blank forms or notarize the papers it records. A title company or attorney handles that.

faqs.q: Is a street address enough for the legal description?
faqs.a: No. Section 59.310 calls for a lot, block and plat, or a metes and bounds or section, township and range description. An address alone is refused.

faqs.q: What does a certified copy of my deed cost?
faqs.a: The county charges $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, plus $1 to certify. A phone order by card adds a $1 card fee and postage.

faqs.q: Do I need planning approval before recording a deed for a small parcel?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A deed for less than 10 acres in an unincorporated area, or part of a subdivision lot, needs a Planning and Zoning exemption before the recorder will take it.
